courses.description: This course is an introductory course for all students which aims to provide an overview on the history, basic concepts and current issues in the field of public health. Students will gain a broad, general understanding on how public health issues can be framed in the three interrelated domains of health protection, health improvement, and health services. This foundation course will equip students with an analytic lens that is essential for deeper learning in each of the three domains.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
For taught postgraduate students in:- 
(i) PgD Health Services Management and Public Health; (ii) PgD Public Health; (iii) MSc Health Education; (iv) Master of Public Health; or 
(v) MBA Health Care
courses.learning_outcomes: Understand the basic concept and characteristics of public health and social determinants of health. Understand the key functions of health system in analyzing public health issues; Understand the basic concept of population, society and global disparities of health and promoting equity; Understand the basic structures of health systems, in particular the challenges of NCDs & communicable diseases; Gain familiarity of concepts of environmental change and global health.

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: Introduction to Qualitative Research: Theories and Research Design
courses.description: This qualitative methods course will introduce students to the topical issues related to conducting qualitative research and allow for hands-on exposure to the methods of data collection and analysis used in this methodology
courses.learning_outcomes:
Student should be able to:

* Understand the definition and features of qualitative research
* Understand the philosophical basis of qualitative approaches and describe its applications
* Understand and apply the skills of conducting qualitative research: case study, observation, interview, focus group, and textual analysis
* Understand and apply the skills of data coding and interpretation in the analytical proce

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: Public Health Law
courses.description: This Course examines the role of law as a tool for public health both within Hong Kong and at international level.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Public Health
courses.learning_outcomes:
Student should be able to:
1. examine the role that law and lawyers play in protecting the public health and in promoting health, including in relation to both communicable and non-communicable disease
2. understand the principles of common law, administrative law, public law and of the legislation which purports to regulate the public health.
3. require consideration of the constitutional limits of the state’s power to impose public health interventions on individuals, and of principles of human rights and ethics that serve to protect the rights and dignity of individuals in the context of public benefit.
4. address the role of the international community in protection of national and global public health.
5. research the law and relevant LegCo papers for yourself
6. understand the structure of a Hong Kong Ordinance
7. analyse the duties and powers of Government Departments relevant to Public Health Law

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: Tuberculosis: Biology, Control and Policy
courses.description: Tuberculosis (TB) has been declared as a public health threat by the WHO since 1990s, and the threat is recently more serious due to rapid development of multi-drug resistant TB and HIV/TB co-infection. The course will introduce TB microbiological, clinical and control aspects, and discuss TB epidemiology, evolution of control programmes, policies and practices both globally and locally. Health system and policy issues on TB control, regarding organisation, financing, payment, delivery will be widely explored. Examples on operational research over TB topics will be given.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For TPg students in Master of Public Health / Postgraduate Diploma in Public Health
courses.learning_outcomes:
Student should be able to:
1. Be familiar of TB biology and epidemiology aspects
2. Understand TB control policies, practice and key partners at the international level.
3. Gain first hand experience of TB control in various countries, including China, UK, Hong Kong, and other high burden
countries in Asia and Africa
4. Understand issues in TB control and its interaction with wider health system issues
5. Be familiar with operational research and able to design operational research for their own programmes

courses.description: This course is a basic introduction to the human body for public health students without a bio-medical background. It is geared towards students with an undergraduate degree in the social sciences, arts and physical sciences. It will introduce the overview of basic scientific mechanisms, concepts and principles in health and in the pathogenesis of disease. It provides clinical scientific foundation for applications to the practice of public health. Professionals in the clinical health field such as physicians, nurses, dentists and allied health specialists will not be permitted to take this course for credit.

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: Practice of Qualitative Research Methods
courses.description: The central goal of this course is to prepare students to enhance their knowledge and skills to design and conduct qualitative research projects and analyse qualitative data. The course begins with an advanced reflection about the theoretical and methodological foundations of different qualitative health research methods. It provides students with hands-on experience of designing an interview protocol, conducting in-depth interview, data analysis, and writing a qualitative report.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For TPg students under School of Public Health
courses.learning_outcomes:
Student should be able to:
1. To demonstrate competency in understanding major methods employed in qualitative research in public health
2. To apply and formulate qualitative methods and skills through the preparation of a research protocol
3. Understand and apply the skills of data collection: observation, in-depth interview, and focus group interview
4. Understand and apply the skills of data coding and interpretation in the analytical process
5. To be familiar with the use of qualitative data analysis software
6. To be able to write a qualitative research paper

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: R Analytics in Environmental Health Sciences
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the R programming environment and commonly used tidyverse packages for data preprocessing and visualization. It will also cover basic applications of biostatistics and modeling packages in R. Students will be assessed through an open-book in-class examination covering the skills taught in the course.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Public Health and MSc Epidemiology and Biostatistics
courses.learning_outcomes:
1) Understand basic coding in R computing environment

2) Apply modern coding concepts and practices through the tidyverse packages

3) Process raw data to prepare it for statistical analysis

4) Present and discuss results using the most suitable visualization and interactive methods

5) Apply the coding skills learned in the course to their own projects

6) Have the capability to independently learn and apply R packages not covered in the course

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: Climate Change and Planetary Health
courses.description: Climate change is an important topic for public health practice. As the frequency and severity of climate-related disasters increase, in order to protect health and well-being, the need to understand and prepare for unforeseeable events is rapidly growing. This course provides an overview of issues in relation to climate change and health in the context of public health practice. It introduces important concepts of how to tackle climate change related health impacts and how to support community preparedness, response, policy formulation and implementation.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For TPg students in Master of Public Health / Postgraduate Diploma in Public Health
courses.learning_outcomes:
After this course, the students will be able to:
1. Gain knowledge in various types of natural disaster and weather-related events, and the relationship between climate change and disasters
2. Associate the change of temperature and rainfall and the transmission of infectious diseases
3. Understand and discuss climate change impact on health in the context of public health
4. Identify key climate change events and existing studies and their link to public health related actions
5. Outline the potential strategies and public health action that can mitigate the adverse health impacts under the extreme weather events or climate-related disasters

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: Development of Assessment instruments and questionnaire design
courses.description: This course aims to provide students with an understanding of the basic principles and procedures in designing questionnaires and health-related assessment instruments. The course includes basic principles and procedures in questionnaire design, psychometrics, validation of an assessment instrument, and related statistical issues. At the completion of the course, students are enabled to develop a simple questionnaire suitable for collecting information for their own research project or in a specific area of their own interest.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For TPg students under School of Public Health

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: Ethics, Social Justice and Global Health
courses.description: This course will introduce students to basic ideas of public health ethics and justice and discusses how those ideas apply to global biomedical issues.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Public Health
courses.learning_outcomes:
Student should be able to:
1. Understand basic ideas about global health ethics and global justice.
2. Understand some key facts about current practices in health care and medical research that have global consequences.
3. Judge the strengths and weaknesses of value arguments in the readings.
4. Express your own ideas and learn how to explain your reasons to other people.

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: International Field Studies
courses.description: This module is designed to allow students to conduct field studies abroad and locally, and to receive academic credit for their supervised work and studies. Field studies may include supervised field visits, public health-related field work, collaborative projects with an organization involving international public health activities . Short courses offered in abroad which require presence in that setting will also be accepted. All projects must receive prior approval from the module coordinator in order to receive credit. All field studies must include some form of assessment that must receive prior approval from the module coordinator. Students are to be selected by the course coordinator and subject to mutual agreement with partner organization.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Public Health
courses.learning_outcomes:
Student should be able to:

* Understand concepts, theories and core issues in health equity
* Learn about the basic methodologies applied in health equity research
* Identify health equity issues in Hong Kong and around the world

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: International Exchange Study
courses.description: Public Health in Action in The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): Field study of Brunei Darussalam’s healthcare system, disease prevention and control strategies
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Public Health and MSc Epidemiology & Biostatistics
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Observe the organisation and delivery of healthcare services in Brunei, and compare them with health service models in other Asia Pacific countries and jurisdictions (including Hong Kong and Mainland China).
2. Explain environmental health and vector control strategies used for vector borne diseases and other infectious diseases.
3. Assess regulatory mechanisms for food safety and worker safety through relevant agencies.
4. Discuss how intersectoral collaboration supports national public health goals, including cross-agency coordination in infectious disease control, environmental health, and safety regulation.
5. Reflect on lessons learned and how insights from Brunei’s public health strategies can inform public health practice in the region.

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: Global Experiential Learning
courses.description: Short-term internships at international organisations: Experiential learning by participating field activities
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Public Health
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Observe the organisation and delivery of public health related programme and projects in Asia-Pacific region.
2. Supplement their academic knowledge with a practical work experience in a field related to the work of hosting organization.
3. Assist in relevant fields in connection to the hosting organization’s strategic framework and to UN Sustainable Development Goals.
4. Participate in high-level discussion on how intersectoral collaboration supports including cross-agency coordination in infectious disease control, One Health, and food safety regulation.
5. Reflect on lessons learned and how insights from Brunei’s public health strategies can inform public health practice in the region.

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: Global and Regional Perspectives on Noncommunicable Diseases Prevention and Control
courses.description: This course aims to provide students an in-depth understanding of the burden of noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) at the local, regional, and global scales. It equips students with the knowledge and tools to prevent and control NCDs and associated risk factors using effective public health strategies, as well as how to conduct NCD surveillance and research to assess and adapt interventions across diverse population settings.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Public Health
courses.learning_outcomes:
After the course, students will be able to
1. describe the NCD burden globally, regionally, and locally, and factors influencing the patterns and trajectories in different population settings.
2. explain common risk factors and determinants of NCDs, and interactions among biological, social, environmental, and modifiable behavioral factors.
3. identify public health strategies, including population and targeted interventions, to address NCDs and risk factors in various populations.
4. discuss success factors and lessons from case studies of population interventions for preventing and controlling high-burden NCDs.
5. demonstrate understanding of common NCD surveillance and research methods, and design a research study proposal for NCD surveillance in a population.

courses.subject: PBHT
courses.title: Practicum
courses.description: The practicum aims at providing a unique opportunity for students to gain familiarity with a variety of public health issues, programs, policies, and service delivery settings. Practicum experience allows students to integrate and apply the knowledge and skills they learned through coursework and prior experiences in a public health environment.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in Master of Public Health.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Discuss key issues of current global health from an application perspective.
2. Expand networking opportunities for future global health career opportunities.
3. Practice and hone presentation skills and participate in case studies.
4. Construct a Mission, Vision, and Values (Personal) Career Statement.
5. List and describe global health leader’s characteristics.
